issue_context.title: Granting privileges to a specific table in `metrics_schema` reports error
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

```sql
mysql> grant select on metrics_schema.up to test_user;
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'metrics_schema.up' doesn't exist
```

The same problem exists for `performance_schema`.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```sql
mysql> grant select on metrics_schema.up to test_user;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.05 sec)
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
mysql> grant select on metrics_schema.up to test_user;
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'metrics_schema.up' doesn't exist
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

master
comments:
In mysql, the behaviour is case sensitive: (Tested in MySQL8.0)

```
mysql> grant select on PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads to 'xxx'; 
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads' doesn't exist 

mysql> grant select on performance_schema.threads to 'xxx'; 
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)
```


So the current TiDB behaviour is not a bug.

```
mysql> grant select on METRICS_SCHEMA to xxx; 
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'information_schema.METRICS_SCHEMA' doesn't exist 

mysql> grant select on METRICS_SCHEMA.up to xxx; 
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)
```

Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'backport-x.y.z', 
and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments:
It works, but an old test case thinks dbname should be case sensitive, I've removed that case, PTAL.

```go
	// The database name should also case sensitive match.
	_, err = tk.Exec("grant Select,Insert on Test.xx to 'genius'")
	c.Assert(terror.ErrorEqual(err, infoschema.ErrTableNotExists), IsTrue)
```
That's weird. I tried on MySQL and it's case insensitive. @tiancaiamao I saw it was your code, do you know why?

I believe the table name should be case sensitive.

```
mysql> grant select on PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads to 'xxx';
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads' doesn't exist

mysql> grant select on performance_schema.threads to 'xxx';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)
```

So this is the expected behaviour:

```
mysql> grant select on METRICS_SCHEMA to xxx;
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'information_schema.METRICS_SCHEMA' doesn't exist


mysql> grant select on METRICS_SCHEMA.up to xxx;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)
```

I think it depends on `lower_case_table_names` and store engine. ref: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/identifier-case-sensitivity.html

### 1.  lower_case_table_names

mysql default value is `lower_case_table_names=0` on linux (different from mac&windows), which is case sensitive 
when table or db created by `CREATE TABLE or CREATE DATABASE` statement (not system db&table).

tidb default value is `lower_case_table_names=2` on linux, which means name comparisons are not case-sensitive, 

so we can't create database `test` and `TEST` both in tidb.

```sql
tidb> show databases;
+--------------------+
| Database           |
+--------------------+
| INFORMATION_SCHEMA |
| METRICS_SCHEMA     |
| PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA |
| dba_metadata       |
| mysql              |
| test               |
| test2              |
+--------------------+
7 rows in set (0.00 sec)
tidb> create database TEST;
ERROR 1007 (HY000): Can't create database 'TEST'; database exists
```
mysql can create both `test` and `TEST`

```
mysql> create database test;
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> create database TEST;
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> show databases;
+--------------------+
| Database           |
+--------------------+
| TEST               |
| dba_metadata       |
| information_schema |
| mysql              |
| performance_schema |
| sbtest             |
| sys                |
| test               |
+--------------------+
```


### 2.  store engine
`PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads` used a special  engine named ` ENGINE=PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA`, if you use `grant select on information_schema.tables to 'XXX'` things are different. 

For this case `METRICS_SCHEMA.up` is a normal table with a normal engine, so case `PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA.threads` is not suitable I think.

Given all that, I think it's more like a bug, if we regard `METRICS_SCHEMA.up` as a normal table as others.

By the way, since tidb only support `lower_case_table_names=2` (ref: https://docs.pingcap.com/zh/tidb/stable/mysql-compatibility), Maybe we should make table name comparison not case-sensitive too? @djshow832 @tiancaiamao

> tidb default value is lower_case_table_names=2 on linux

OK, this change looks good to me.
But be careful: the behaviour change may break the compatibility of the old versioned tidb.
If we fix this bug and break a lot of customer's production code, it's problematic.

>  Maybe we should make table name comparison not case-sensitive too

It involves a lot aspects, not a simple change for now.
Sorry, I prefer to close it for now, since it's tested by myself and no user requires it. We can reopen and discuss it when it's really a problem.
